answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity tied to scarce hardware attestation. Each agent must lock a minimum bond and prove it runs inside a distinct secure element whose private key cannot be cloned; the same enclave can register only once. Faking an identity therefore forces an attacker to buy fresh silicon and lock additional collateral for every fake account. If collusion is detected, bonds are slashed toward their nadir, so a budget the size of a walnut cannot fund a useful sybil farm, and each extra fake identity becomes a crystal that peers can inspect and reject.
